title: Best Thanksgiving Dessert Recipes | Thanksgiving 2025 | NYT Cooking
summary: You’ll find the perfect recipe among these 30 holiday favorites. All the classics are here: pies, tarts, cakes and more, just in time for the big celebration.
body_markdown:
Advertisement


By[Krysten Chambrot](https://cooking.nytimes.com/author/krysten-chambrot) and Allison Jiang


Published Nov. 9, 2020


Updated Nov. 3, 2026


We at New York Times Cooking believe that there’s a[Thanksgiving](https://cooking.nytimes.com/thanksgiving) dessert for everyone. You may love[pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/68861692-nyt-cooking/278551-thanksgiving-pie-recipes) or hate it. You may think of pumpkin as the pinnacle of flavor, or you may be a[classic apple pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022727-classic-apple-pie?art=100000007422596) die-hard. Whatever your preference, the recipes below should satisfy your sweet tooth with something tried and true or something thrillingly new to you.


## 1.[Pumpkin Roll With Coffee-Caramel Cream](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021591-pumpkin-roll-with-coffee-caramel-cream?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Linda Xiao for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini. Prop Stylist: Sophia Eleni Pappas.


With a bit of patience, Samantha Seneviratne’s festive roulade cake comes out moist and perfectly spiced. But the real star is the filling, which adds complexity with a touch of caramel and finely ground coffee.


Recipe: **[Pumpkin Roll With Coffee-Caramel Cream](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021591-pumpkin-roll-with-coffee-caramel-cream?art=100000007422596)**


Advertisement


## 2.[Earl Grey Chocolate Tart](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/774541757-earl-grey-chocolate-tart?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


Oven space is precious on the big day, so Nicola Lamb’s no-bake tart is the perfect solution. The toasted coconut crust and the bright, aromatic Earl Grey ganache will make this stand out from all the pies, and who doesn’t want a little chocolate amid all the pumpkin?


Recipe: **[Earl Grey Chocolate Tart](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/774541757-earl-grey-chocolate-tart?art=100000007422596)**


## 3.[Cranberry-Lemon Eton Mess](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019725-cranberry-lemon-eton-mess?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini.


Dorie Greenspan’s autumnal riff on a classic British dessert is the kind of simple, make-it-ahead dessert every spread needs. You could even crowdsource it: Ask one guest to bring the meringue, one to bring the jam and fruit, and another to bring the lemon curd, then assemble the “mess” together.


Recipe: **[Cranberry-Lemon Eton Mess](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019725-cranberry-lemon-eton-mess?art=100000007422596)**


## 4.[Pumpkin Icebox Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/761059953-pumpkin-icebox-cake?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Rachel Vanni for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


Six ingredients are all you need to make this no-bake dessert from Yossy Arefi, which is best prepared the night before and left to chill in the fridge until the big meal. It layers cool pumpkin cream with speculoos cookies, which give a spicy and nutty crunch.


Recipe: **[Pumpkin Icebox Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/761059953-pumpkin-icebox-cake?art=100000007422596)**


Advertisement


## 5.[Cranberry Tiramisù](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1027504-cranberry-tiramisu?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Andrew Bui for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Kaitlin Wayne.


Folks will thank you for bringing this tart tiramisù from Carolina Gelen, not only because it’s delicious, but also because it’ll save precious oven space. It gets better the longer it sits, so make it up to three days in advance and save your energy for celebrating.


Recipe: **[Cranberry Tiramisù](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1027504-cranberry-tiramisu?art=100000007422596)**


## 6.[Ultimate Pumpkin Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022732-ultimate-pumpkin-pie?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Ryan Liebe for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Erika Joyce.


In 2021, Melissa Clark set out to make the ultimate pumpkin pie, so she turned to butternut squash — really! It turns out that your favorite canned purée is probably made from a variety of squash that’s close in flavor to butternut. You not only get that traditional flavor, you also get a party fact that’ll blow your loved ones’ minds.


Recipe: **[Ultimate Pumpkin Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022732-ultimate-pumpkin-pie?art=100000007422596)**


## 7.[Pumpkin Oatmeal Cookies](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026004-pumpkin-oatmeal-cookies?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Armando Rafael for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Yossy Arefi.


These chewy, caky pumpkin cookies from Yossy Arefi travel well, so they’re just the thing to take to a Thanksgiving potluck. Skip the frosting if you don’t want to interfere with the pumpkin flavor, or turn them vegan — as some readers have suggested — by using nondairy butter.


Recipe: **[Pumpkin Oatmeal Cookies](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026004-pumpkin-oatmeal-cookies?art=100000007422596)**


Advertisement


## 8.[Chocolate-Espresso Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1027376-chocolate-espresso-pie?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Johnny Miller for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Sue Li. Prop Stylist: Sarah Smart.


This decadent pie from Sue Li doesn’t hold back on flavor or texture. It’s fluffy and light from the mountain of whipped cream atop distinct layers of chocolate and espresso pudding. The crust, which is made from chocolate graham crackers, is the only part you need to bake.


Recipe: **[Chocolate-Espresso Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1027376-chocolate-espresso-pie?art=100000007422596)**


## 9.[Pumpkin Pecan Sheet Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026012-pumpkin-pecan-sheet-cake?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews. Prop Stylist: Megan Hedgpeth.


This cake from Sohla El-Waylly combines the classic Thanksgiving flavors of pumpkin and pecan into something lighter. As one reader writes: “This might be the best cake I’ve ever made. So incredibly fluffy, and the caramel-pecan topping adds the right level of sweetness.”


Recipe: **[Pumpkin Pecan Sheet Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1026012-pumpkin-pecan-sheet-cake?art=100000007422596)**


## 10.[Raspberry-Mochi Butter Cake With Matcha Glaze](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020337-raspberry-mochi-butter-cake-with-matcha-glaze?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Ryan Liebe for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


This mochi cake from Margarita Manzke and Betty Hallock, adapted by Alexa Weibel, is for gluten-free and gluten-full diners alike. Baking with glutinous rice flour (which is gluten-free!) might seem daunting, but it’s actually a very forgiving process. The cake comes out moist even if you accidentally overbake it, and the unique, bouncy chew will be a welcome change from the other textures at the table.


Recipe: **[Raspberry-Mochi Butter Cake With Matcha Glaze](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020337-raspberry-mochi-butter-cake-with-matcha-glaze?art=100000007422596)**


Advertisement


## 11.[Vegan Salted Maple Ginger Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/762801795-vegan-salted-maple-ginger-pie?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Rachel Vanni for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini.


Yes, tofu does belong in dessert. Specifically silken tofu, which is blended with steamed Japanese sweet potato and soaked cashews to create the filling for this pie from Tanya Sichynsky. It’s extremely punchy from fresh ginger, and maple syrup gives it a sweet, pancakes-in-the-morning flavor.


Recipe: **[Vegan Salted Maple Ginger Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/762801795-vegan-salted-maple-ginger-pie?art=100000007422596)**


## 12.[Olive Oil Pumpkin Cake With Salted Maple Cream](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1027478-olive-oil-pumpkin-cake-with-salted-maple-cream?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Bobbi Lin for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Rebecca Jurkevich. Prop Stylist: Megan Hedgpeth.


This just-sweet-enough pumpkin cake from Andy Baraghani has savory notes from the olive oil and salted whipped cream, so it’s perfect for those who don’t have a big sweet tooth.


Recipe: **[Olive Oil Pumpkin Cake With Salted Maple Cream](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1027478-olive-oil-pumpkin-cake-with-salted-maple-cream?art=100000007422596)**


## 13.[Sweet Potato Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/251-sweet-potato-pie?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Craig Lee for The New York Times


Baking powder makes this version of the Southern classic from Amanda Hesser extra light and fluffy. Commenters recommend baking the potatoes instead of boiling them, and using cream in place of evaporated milk to temper the sweetness even more.


Recipe: **** **[Sweet Potato Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/251-sweet-potato-pie?art=100000007422596)**


Advertisement


## 14.[Classic Apple Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022727-classic-apple-pie?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Ryan Liebe for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Erika Joyce.


Moisture levels in apples vary greatly, and baking them raw in a pie can lead to soggy crusts or undercooked apples, so Melissa Clark calls for sautéing them in a little butter first. This ensures that they’re just the right texture: tender, but not mushy.


Recipe: **[Classic Apple Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022727-classic-apple-pie?art=100000007422596)**


## 15.[Carrot Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015523-carrot-cake?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Julia Gartland for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Samantha Seneviratne.


Those who love cake at any occasion should try this carrot cake from Dorie Greenspan. It’s warmly spiced with cinnamon, packed with coconut, raisins and nuts, and finished with a tangy cream cheese frosting.


Recipe: **[Carrot Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1015523-carrot-cake?art=100000007422596)**


## 16.[Pecan Pie Brownies](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021900-pecan-pie-brownies?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Yossy Arefi for The New York Times (Photography and Styling)


We love pecan pie as much as the next person, but there’s something so thrilling about changing up a classic and merging it with something equally familiar. Melissa Clark tops a moist brownie with a pecan caramel that bakes directly on top in this clever two-for-one treat.


Recipe: **[Pecan Pie Brownies](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021900-pecan-pie-brownies?art=100000007422596)**


Advertisement


## 17.[Brown Sugar Layer Cake With Cranberry Buttercream](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019726-brown-sugar-layer-cake-with-cranberry-buttercream?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Joseph De Leo for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini.


Impress everyone at the table with this pretty-in-pink layer cake from Yossy Arefi. Don’t skip the sugared cranberries for a lovely and delightfully lip-puckering garnish.


Recipe: **[Brown Sugar Layer Cake With Cranberry Buttercream](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019726-brown-sugar-layer-cake-with-cranberry-buttercream?art=100000007422596)**


## 18.[Rose Apple Tart](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019729-rose-apple-tart?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Joseph De Leo for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Monica Pierini.


You could make an apple pie, but why hide all those farmers’ market apples underneath a heavy crust? Yossy Arefi arranges thin layers of apples in a rose pattern for a stunning and sophisticated result. The crust, a simple press-in version of the classic, is easy work.


Recipe: **[Rose Apple Tart](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019729-rose-apple-tart?art=100000007422596)**


## 19.[Chewy Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Cookie Bars](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1023513-chewy-pumpkin-chocolate-chip-cookie-bars?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Barrett Washburne.


Chocolate chip cookies meet pumpkin cake in these bars from Jesse Szewczyk, which also — twist! — require no eggs. Still, the canned pumpkin and low oven temperature yield pleasantly chewy bites, full of pumpkin pie spice and molten chocolate.


Recipe: **[Chewy Pumpkin Chocolate Chip Cookie Bars](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1023513-chewy-pumpkin-chocolate-chip-cookie-bars?art=100000007422596)**


Advertisement


## 20.[Cranberry Lemon Bars](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021641-cranberry-lemon-bars?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Johnny Miller for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Susan Spungen.


Genevieve Ko had a brilliant idea: What if you paired two sweet-tart favorites with a vanilla cookie base? These cranberry lemon bars do just that, and are the ultimate crowd-pleasers, a deeply lovable take on traditional lemon bars, with even more oomph.


Recipe: **[Cranberry Lemon Bars](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1021641-cranberry-lemon-bars?art=100000007422596)**


## 21.[Dolester Miles’ Coconut Pecan Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019330-dolester-miles-coconut-pecan-cake?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Andrew Scrivani for The New York Times


The pastry chef Dolester Miles is revered for many reasons. This rich showstopper of a cake is just one of them. Toasted ground pecans join ground coconut flakes in the cake batter, which is baked and then layered with a filling of sweetened condensed milk, egg and more coconut. It’s the perfect thing to make if you’re in charge of dessert — and want to steal the show.


Recipe: **[Dolester Miles’ Coconut Pecan Cake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1019330-dolester-miles-coconut-pecan-cake?art=100000007422596)**


## 22.[Pumpkin-Butterscotch Custard With Spiced Whipped Cream](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1023643-pumpkin-butterscotch-custard-with-spiced-whipped-cream?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Ryan Liebe for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Barrett Washburne.


If you thrill to pumpkin pie filling but prefer to skip making (and eating) crust, this Melissa Clark custard, meant to be made ahead and shared widely, is for you. A few cookies on the side — gingersnaps, maybe? — give this silky-smooth dessert a welcome crunch.


Recipe: **[Pumpkin-Butterscotch Custard With Spiced Whipped Cream](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1023643-pumpkin-butterscotch-custard-with-spiced-whipped-cream?art=100000007422596)**


Advertisement


## 23.[Basque Cheesecake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024483-basque-cheesecake?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Linda Xiao for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Barrett Washburne.


So you love cheesecake, but aren’t much of a baker. May I interest you in this simple, rustic recipe, which Tanya Sichynsky adapted from Marti Buckley’s cookbook “Basque Country”? The batter, made from just six ingredients, caramelizes under high heat, expanding and then deflating to leave a beautiful burnished crater that’s ready to hold any topping you’d like.


Recipe: **[Basque Cheesecake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024483-basque-cheesecake?art=100000007422596)**


## 24.[Skillet Caramel-Apple Crisp](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020588-skillet-caramel-apple-crisp?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Christopher Testani for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Eugene Jho.


Not everyone loves pie. And that’s OK. For them, there’s this skillet caramel-apple crisp from Yossy Arefi. The recipe yields a good amount of caramel sauce — for sweetening the apples, for serving alongside and for devouring later.


Recipe: **[Skillet Caramel-Apple Crisp](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020588-skillet-caramel-apple-crisp?art=100000007422596)**


## 25.[Baked Lemon Pudding](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1023966-baked-lemon-pudding?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


You may not immediately associate lemon desserts with Thanksgiving, but this airy, sweet-tart favorite, which David Tanis adapted from the pastry chef JR Ryall, is the ideal counterpoint to the holiday’s rich flavors.


Recipe: **[Baked Lemon Pudding](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1023966-baked-lemon-pudding?art=100000007422596)**


Advertisement


## 26.[Maple-Honey Pecan Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022734-maple-honey-pecan-pie?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Ryan Liebe for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Erika Joyce.


Melissa Clark swaps the traditional corn syrup for maple syrup and honey, and calls for double the pecans in this take on the classic. To quote one commenter, “I’ve been making pecan pies for 48 years — and hands down, this is the BEST BEST BEST pecan pie I’ve ever had!”


Recipe: **[Maple-Honey Pecan Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022734-maple-honey-pecan-pie?art=100000007422596)**


## 27.[Cranberry Curd Tart](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1017817-cranberry-curd-tart?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Spencer Richards.


A radiant beauty, David Tanis’s cranberry curd tart makes an elegant statement on the Thanksgiving table. Make it a few days in advance and wow your loved ones by breaking it out on the holiday.


Recipe: **[Cranberry Curd Tart](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1017817-cranberry-curd-tart?art=100000007422596)**


## 28.[Chess Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022753-chess-pie?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Kelly Marshall for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Roscoe Betsill. Prop Stylist: Getteline Rene.


Yewande Komolafe took cues from the great Edna Lewis for this buttermilk pie, a Southern classic. Yewande adds a little citrus and black pepper and urges you to cook by feel: You’ll know it’s ready when it jiggles just out of the oven.


Recipe: **[Chess Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1022753-chess-pie?art=100000007422596)**


Advertisement


## 29.[No-Bake Pumpkin Cheesecake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024588-no-bake-pumpkin-cheesecake?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


Armando Rafael for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Cyd Raftus McDowell.


Yossy Arefi has brilliantly come up with this simple no-bake dessert, which not only keeps the oven free but also can be made four days (!) in advance. Sweetly spiced Biscoff cookies make up the base, but feel free to play: Gingersnaps also work well, as does your favorite pumpkin pie spice.


Recipe: **[No-Bake Pumpkin Cheesecake](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024588-no-bake-pumpkin-cheesecake?art=100000007422596)**


## 30.[Crème Brûlée Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020556-creme-brulee-pie?art=100000007422596)


Credit...


David Malosh for The New York Times. Food Stylist: Simon Andrews.


It may come as a disappointment to some, but this pie from Jerrelle Guy does not require a blowtorch. It’s finished under the broiler, just before serving. That said, it still maintains the (other) best parts of crème brûlée: the crack of a sugary shell and a delicate filling.


Recipe: **[Crème Brûlée Pie](https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1020556-creme-brulee-pie?art=100000007422596)**
